newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks rally to record on second-quarter hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks rally to record on second-quarter hopes.

text.p: Mexican stocks chalked up their third record close in a row on Thursday to end a hair below the 4,000 point mark, which they earlier crossed for the first time ever.
Dealers and analysts said investors bought on market forecasts that a recent slew of positive economic figures would finally translate into improvements in company earnings during the second quarter.

The leading IPC share index ended up 25.10 points, or 0.63 percent, at 3,999.52. In the broad market, of 108 stocks traded, gains outnumbered losses 52 to 43 on restrained volume of 84.7 million shares.

"Domestic rates are low and the outlook for second quarter earnings is better, at least on the operating line, and we see economic indicators improving, too," said Esteban Rojas, associate research director at the Arka brokerage.
Rojas said the bourse eased off its record high on profit-taking.
"It tested firm resistance, which we think it could break through next week," he said.
Dealers said profit-taking was most notable on telecommunications company Telmex and financial group Bancomer, which together accounted for some 30 percent of all shares traded.

Nonetheless, Bancomer posted sharp gains and outweighed Telmex's losses at the close. Bancomer ended up six centavos (less than one cent) to 3.10 pesos (39 cents), while Telmex slid two centavos (less than one cent) to 17.44 pesos ($2.21), in tandem with its American Depositary Receipts, which lost 25 cents to $44.375.
"There was a bit of profit-taking and maybe some skittishness also because of the Dow's late downturn," a trader said.
The Dow Jones industrial average closed down 32.56 points at 7,258.13.

Earlier, Banco de Mexico said the Consumer Price Index rose 0.48 percent from May 1 to May 15, less than an average forecast of a 0.53 percent rise, according to a Reuters survey of Mexico City financial houses.
Dealers said one sector that missed out on the rally was retail stocks, which were hit by slow sales figures released late on Wednesday.
The Elektra retail chain, for example, fell 70 centavos (nine cents) to 75.30 pesos ($9.55).
